question: A rectangular tank measures 12 cm long, 10 cm wide, and 6 cm high. If a spherical ball of the largest possible size is placed inside this tank, what is the volume of the space not occupied by the ball?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The diameter of the largest possible sphere equals the smallest dimension of the rectangular tank.

⇒ Diameter = 6 cm ⇒ Radius = 3 cm

⇒ Unoccupied Space = Volume of Tank − Volume of Sphere

⇒ Unoccupied Space = (12 × 10 × 6) − (4/3 × π × 3³)

⇒ Unoccupied Space = (720 − 36π) cm³

**∴ The correct answer is (720-36π) cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the rectangular tank (L) = 12 cm

Width of the rectangular tank (W) = 10 cm

Height of the rectangular tank (H) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a Cuboid = L × W × H

Volume of a Sphere = 4/3 × π × r³

 
• Length = 12 cm 
• Height = 6 cm 
• r = 3 cm Front View of Tank and Sphere 

**Calculations:**

⇒ The largest spherical ball that can fit entirely inside the tank must have a diameter equal to the smallest dimension of the tank to avoid overlapping the boundaries.

⇒ Smallest dimension among 12 cm, 10 cm, and 6 cm is 6 cm.

⇒ Diameter of the sphere = 6 cm

⇒ Radius of the sphere (r) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Volume of the rectangular tank = L × W × H

⇒ Volume of the rectangular tank = 12 × 10 × 6 = 720 cm³

⇒ Volume of the spherical ball = 4/3 × π × r³

⇒ Volume of the spherical ball = 4/3 × π × (3)³ = 4/3 × π × 27 = 36π cm³

⇒ Volume of the space not occupied = Volume of the tank − Volume of the spherical ball

⇒ Unoccupied volume = (720 − 36π) cm³

**∴ The correct answer is (720-36π) cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone with base radius r and vertical height h is given by V = 1/3 × π × r² × h.

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume of a right circular cylinder with base radius r and height h is given by V = π × r² × h.

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere with radius r is given by A = 4 × π × r².

Largest Sphere inside a Cube

For a cube of side a, the largest sphere that can be placed inside it has a diameter exactly equal to the side length a, meaning its radius = a/2.
